name: Bali Safari & Marine Park
description: Family-friendly park with underwater exhibits, interactive experiences, animal encounters and educational presentations.
tips: Carry a hat and sunscreen and keep a water bottle handy
A stroller is useful for children who tire easily
Check show and activity timings on arrival as performances depend on schedules and conditions

name: Ubud Palace
description: Former royal residence at the heart of Ubud, a compact complex with ornate gateways, carved stonework and traditional courtyards; a good introduction to Balinese royal architecture.
dress_code: Dress respectfully; shoulders and knees covered
tips: Allow time for photographs of carved gates and courtyards

name: Tirta Empul Temple
description: Sacred Balinese Hindu temple founded over a thousand years ago, known for its holy spring water and purification pools
dress_code: Modest clothing recommended; sarongs are generally provided at the entrance
tips: Carry a change of clothes to take part in the holy spring purification ritual
Women who are menstruating are not permitted to enter the temple premises

name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
description: Signature layered rice paddies stepping down a valley.
tips: The swings are optional; the landscape is the attraction

name: Tirta Empul Temple
description: One of Bali's most sacred water temples, famous for its holy spring water and traditional purification rituals.
tips: Women on their menstruation cycle are not permitted to enter the temple

name: Bali Safari & Marine Park
description: Home to hundreds of animals from Indonesia, India, and Africa across beautifully landscaped grounds. Jungle Hopper Package includes safari journey, animal encounters, educational presentations, and selected park attractions.
entry_fee: Approx. INR 4,000–6,000 per person (depending on package selected)

name: Blue Lagoon
description: Viewpoint with dramatic limestone cliffs and striking turquoise water, best in good weather.
tips: Cliff edges are exposed, so treat it as a look-and-photograph stop

name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
description: One of Bali's signature agricultural landscapes, with terraces cascading down the valley in layers of green; mainly a scenic and photographic stop.
tips: Wear comfortable footwear as paths can be uneven
Carry sunscreen, hats and water as afternoons can be warm
Swings, café food and drinks are optional and paid separately
